    StartersShort Round's samosasCrisp fried cones of potato and peas. Hold on to your potatoes.How to make it500g potatoes, diced150g frozen peas1 tsp ground cumin1 red chilli, chopped1 tsp garam masala250g plain flour3 tbsp vegetable oil, for the dough1 L vegetable oil, for frying4 tbsp tamarind chutneysalt, to tasteMix the flour with the dough oil, salt and enough water into a stiff dough. Rest while you cook the filling.Cook the potatoes until tender, then toss with the peas, cumin, chilli, garam masala and salt.Roll the dough, cut and shape into cones, fill and seal.Fry at 175°C until blistered and golden, in batches.Serve with tamarind chutney.Coiled chipolata snake with mango glazeChipolatas coiled into a snake, glazed with mango chutney and chilli, yoghurt dipHow to make it500g chipolatas3 tbsp mango chutney1 red chilli, chopped200g Greek yoghurt1/2 tsp ground cuminCoil the chipolatas tightly on a tray, pinning with skewers.Brush with mango chutney mixed with the chilli. Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes.Stir the cumin into the yoghurt and serve alongside. Surprise.MainsMaharaja's lamb curryYoghurt marinated lamb shoulder braised with onions and tomatoHow to make it1.2kg lamb shoulder, diced200g Greek yoghurt1 piece ginger, 4cm, grated3 garlic cloves, crushed2 tsp garam masala3 brown onions, sliced1 tin crushed tomatoes2 tbsp vegetable oil300g basmati ricesalt, to tasteMix the lamb with the yoghurt, ginger, garlic and garam masala.Marinate overnight in the fridge.Cook the onions slowly in oil until deep brown.Add the tomatoes, then the lamb with its marinade, and season with salt to taste. Cover and braise at 160°C for 2 hours 30 minutes.Cook the rice and serve with the curry.Mayapore village thaliThe village whose sacred stone was takenHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chickpeas in tomato onion masala, yellow dal tempered with mustard seed and cumin, turmeric roasted cauliflower, basmati, warm flatbread and mango pickle.Simmer 200g yellow split peas with turmeric in 1L water for 40 minutes, then pour over 1 tsp mustard seeds and 1 tsp cumin sizzled in 2 tbsp ghee.Soften an onion with garlic, ginger and 2 tsp garam masala, add 400g tomatoes and 2 tins chickpeas and simmer 20 minutes.Roast a cauliflower in florets with turmeric and oil at 220°C for 25 minutes.Cook 300g basmati.Warm 4 flatbreads and serve with mango pickle.SweetsChilled mango brainsMango puree and whipped cream set in dome moulds, turned out chilledHow to make it2 mangoes60g caster sugar4 gelatine leaves250ml thickened cream, whipped2 passionfruitsBlitz the mangoes with the sugar into a purée.Soak the gelatine leaves in cold water, then dissolve in a little warm purée and stir through the rest.Fold in the whipped cream and spoon into dome moulds.Set in the fridge for 4 hours.Turn out and top with passionfruit pulp.DrinksSankara stone saffron mango lassiMango, yoghurt, honey, cardamom and saffron blended with milkHow to make it1 pinch saffron1 tbsp warm milk2 ripe mangoes400g natural yoghurt400ml cold milk2 tbsp honey1 pinch ground cardamom30g pistachios, crushed2 cups iceSoak the saffron in the warm milk for 10 minutes.Blend the mangoes with the yoghurt, cold milk, honey, cardamom and saffron milk until smooth and frothy.Pour over ice into four glasses and top with crushed pistachios.
